checks.title: Analyzers are wired in and runnable by one command
checks.why: Analyzer rules are this stack's written-down conventions in a form a machine can enforce. Configured but only visible inside an IDE means an agent never sees them.
checks.ask: Are analyzers enforced by the build here, and does one command run them?

checks.title: A script stands up a running instance with this project installed
checks.why: An agent that cannot start the product cannot check its change by hand or run anything end to end. This is the single biggest difference between a repo the loops do good work in and one they do not.
checks.ask: What stands up a running instance of the product with this project installed?

checks.title: A restore in a fresh worktree needs no credential
checks.why: A restore that needs a feed credential fails inside the bare worktree the default ops-workspace creates, and the failure reads as a broken build rather than a missing secret.
checks.ask: Does restoring this repo need a credential for a private package feed?
